The Complete Claude Guide for Product Managers: 42 Claude Skills for the Whole Product Job

Forty-two skills that follow the product job in the order you do it: set direction, discover, decide, define, deliver, launch, prove, then run the product. Each one keeps a single framework, says where it breaks, and names the next skill to run.

01What these skills are

The product job, as installable Claude skills

This is Claude for the whole product job, stage by stage: the direction set, the customers heard, the backlog decided, the work defined, delivered, launched and then proved — plus the weekly rhythm that keeps it all running.

The skills follow the job in eight stages, in the order the work happens, and each stage hands a named artifact to the next.

The red line: real customers are not optional. Claude drafts the documents, the team talks to users, and a named person makes the call.

Each skill is named as an action and keeps one framework inside, with a fixed output template and the next skill to run.

No invented facts: a missing figure becomes a bracketed placeholder or an open question. Work is scored, people are not, and personas are composites rather than profiles of real people.

Where a skill fits a Claude surface, it says so, and beta features are marked beta.

Download all 42 skills

One zip: ready-to-install skill zips, readable SKILL.md files, and the sources behind every method.

Download the zip

Install in Claude Code

Two lines, and every skill in the pack loads at once.

/plugin marketplace add polar-bear-org/claude-skills
/plugin install complete-claude-guide-for-product-managers-pack@90n-skills

Using Claude on the web instead? Download the zip above and upload each skill from its install folder under Customize → Skills.

02The catalog

The 42 skills you get

The set follows the product job, in eight stages: setting direction, discovering, deciding, defining, delivering, launching, proving — and running the product week to week.

1 · Set direction

1

Write the Product Vision

Use when
The team cannot say in one sentence what it is building toward
Output
Vision statement options, Product Vision Board (target group, needs, product, business goals)
2

Write the Product Strategy

Use when
Everything is high priority and leaders set the roadmap by preference
Output
Diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent actions, “we will not” list
3

Map the Impact

Use when
The roadmap is a feature list and nobody can say whose behaviour each item changes
Output
Goal, actors, impacts, deliverables, the deliverables no impact needs marked to cut
4

Size the Market (TAM, SAM, SOM)

Use when
Leadership asks how big this is and the slide needs a number you can defend
Output
Top-down and bottom-up estimates, sourced assumptions, a range, sanity checks
5

Fill the Lean Canvas

Use when
A new product or bet needs its business logic on one page
Output
One-page business logic, riskiest assumptions marked untested
6

Pick the North Star Metric

Use when
The team ships a lot and cannot say which number it is moving
Output
North star, three to five named inputs with definitions, counter-metrics
7

Build the Product Roadmap

Use when
The roadmap is run from the CEO's inbox and every date becomes a promise
Output
Now-next-later board, confidence notes, “not on the roadmap” list, one-page executive version

2 · Discover

8

Prepare the Customer Interview Guide

Use when
You have 30 minutes with a customer and cannot waste it on opinions
Output
Screener lines, story-based questions, probes, consent note, notes template
9

Synthesise the Interviews

Use when
Five interview transcripts and a PRD due Friday
Output
Affinity clusters, need statements with sources, contradictions, open questions
10

Build the Personas

Use when
The team argues about “the user” and everyone means someone different
Output
Composite personas from interview evidence, each claim linked to its source
11

Map the Customer Journey

Use when
Each team owns a slice and nobody sees where customers drop off
Output
Stages, actions, thoughts and feelings, pain points, opportunities, evidence per cell
12

Map the Jobs to Be Done

Use when
A request arrives with no known job behind it
Output
Job statements, circumstances, forces for and against switching, alternatives
13

Fill the Value Proposition Canvas

Use when
Marketing, sales and product each describe the product differently
Output
Customer profile, value map, fit notes, one positioning line every team uses
14

Build the Opportunity Solution Tree

Use when
Discovery keeps getting squeezed and has to fit between sprints
Output
Outcome, opportunities, target opportunity, three ideas, riskiest assumption per idea

3 · Decide

15

Triage the Feature Requests

Use when
Sales promised it, a big client wants it, the CEO forwarded it, all this week
Output
Request log, the job behind each request, build / later / no sort, reply drafts
16

Score the Backlog with RICE

Use when
40 requests, room for 5, and the loudest voice keeps winning
Output
Scored backlog, confidence notes, out-of-order exceptions, cut list
17

Score with ICE

Use when
Forty growth ideas and one afternoon to pick what to test
Output
Impact, confidence and ease scores, evidence behind each confidence score, top ten to test
18

Rank with WSJF

Use when
Several teams share one backlog and need one order they can defend
Output
Cost of delay parts divided by job size, ranked list, sensitivity check
19

Cost the Delay

Use when
Everything is urgent and you need a no that holds
Output
Urgency profiles, CD3 order, “yes, if” options, reply to the asker
20

Make the Business Case

Use when
You must argue for a feature in finance language and the ROI numbers are guesses
Output
One-page case in five parts, assumptions table with ranges and owners, what would change the answer
21

Set Up the DACI Decision

Use when
Sign-off never comes, or comes and is reversed next week
Output
Driver, approver, contributors, informed, inputs, decision date
22

Keep the Decision Log

Use when
Settled calls keep coming back as if nobody decided
Output
Dated records (context, decision, status, consequences), reopening rule

4 · Define

23

Write the One-Pager

Use when
An idea needs one page before anyone writes a PRD
Output
Problem, who it is for, why now, the bet, success, what we will not do, the ask
24

Write the PR/FAQ

Use when
A prototype is already built and nobody wrote down why
Output
One-page press release, customer FAQ, internal FAQ
25

Write the Prototype Brief

Use when
Leadership saw the AI demo and thinks it ships next week
Output
The belief it tests, pass line set in advance, what it does not prove, gap-to-production list
26

Write the PRD

Use when
The last spec was read five different ways, or the AI draft runs to 12 pages
Output
Problem and evidence, goals, non-goals, numbered testable requirements, open questions, success measures
27

Spec the AI Feature

Use when
Stakeholders expect it to be right every time, and one prompt fix breaks another case
Output
Task, measurable success criteria, acceptable error rate, eval set plan, human fallback, launch bar

5 · Deliver

28

Build the Story Map

Use when
The backlog is 200 tickets and nobody can see the whole product
Output
User activity backbone, walking skeleton, release slices
29

Write the User Stories

Use when
Engineers say the requirements are thin but not what is missing
Output
Stories, Given / When / Then criteria, INVEST check, refinement questions
30

Plan the Sprint

Use when
The sprint is filled to a date promised upstairs and the team never sized the work
Output
Sprint goal as an outcome, capacity by role, items the team selected, definition of done check
31

Run the Sprint Review

Use when
The review is a demo nobody outside the team attends
Output
Increment against the sprint goal, feedback, backlog changes, short key-updates deck
32

Cut Scope with MoSCoW

Use when

Output
Must / Should / Could / Won't list, Must budget check, Won't-this-time list

6 · Launch

33

Write the Competitive Analysis

Use when
Sales keeps saying “the competitor has it”
Output
Landscape table with sources, win / loss themes, where you differ, what not to copy
34

Plan the Go-to-Market

Use when
The product is ready and sales, support and marketing are not
Output
Launch tier, audiences, positioning line, readiness by team, enablement brief
35

Run the Pre-Mortem

Use when
The launch date was promised before anyone asked what could go wrong
Output
Failure story, reasons list, top risks with owners and signals, go / adjust / stop

Write the Release Notes

Use when
Support hears about changes from customers
Output

7 · Prove

37

Set the Success Metrics

Use when
You celebrated a release and still cannot say whether it worked
Output
HEART table (goals, signals, metrics), baseline, target, guardrail
38

Design the Experiment

Use when
Two options, a strong opinion on each side, and enough users to test
Output
Hypothesis, variants, primary metric, guardrails, sample and duration check, decision rule
39

Run the Post-Launch Review

Use when
Two weeks after launch customers still use the old workflow
Output
Intended versus actual, why, keep / change list, keep, fix or remove call

8 · Run the product

40

Write the Weekly Update

Use when
Friday goes on an update people skim, then ask the same questions in three meetings
Output
News-first subject line, bottom line and asks, shipped, at risk, decisions by date, one cut per audience
41

Run the Retro

Use when
The retro raises the same problems every sprint and the actions belong to no one
Output
Last action checked, a format for this cycle, themes, one owned change with a check date
42

Plan the Quarter

Use when
The quarter starts, the goals are a feature list, and every date becomes a promise
Output
Objectives and key results, capacity split, bets, what is out, check-in dates

03How to use it

Pick the workflow that matches your week

No fixed order. Bring the stage you are stuck on. Every skill lists the inputs it needs, so it tells you when the stage before is the one that is missing.

Set direction

Nobody can say what the product is building toward.

  1. Write the Product Vision
  2. Write the Product Strategy
  3. Pick the North Star Metric
  4. Build the Product Roadmap

Hear customers

You have calls to run, or transcripts to read back.

  1. Prepare the Customer Interview Guide
  2. Synthesise the Interviews
  3. Map the Jobs to Be Done
  4. Build the Opportunity Solution Tree

Decide the backlog

The backlog is the problem.

  1. Triage the Feature Requests
  2. Score the Backlog with RICE
  3. Set Up the DACI Decision
  4. Keep the Decision Log

Define the work

The work is chosen and not yet written down.

  1. Write the One-Pager
  2. Write the PR/FAQ
  3. Write the Prototype Brief
  4. Write the PRD
  5. Spec the AI Feature

Deliver it

The work is defined and the sprint is next.

  1. Build the Story Map
  2. Write the User Stories
  3. Plan the Sprint
  4. Run the Sprint Review
  5. Cut Scope with MoSCoW

Launch it

The release is next week.

  1. Write the Competitive Analysis
  2. Plan the Go-to-Market
  3. Run the Pre-Mortem
  4. Write the Release Notes

Prove it worked

You shipped it and still cannot say whether it worked.

  1. Set the Success Metrics
  2. Design the Experiment
  3. Run the Post-Launch Review

04Setup guide

Install it in five minutes

In Claude Code · two lines

/plugin marketplace add polar-bear-org/claude-skills
/plugin install complete-claude-guide-for-product-managers-pack@90n-skills

In Claude.ai or Claude Desktop · seven clicks

  1. 1

    Download the pack, then open Settings

    Unzip the pack: its skills folder holds all 42 skills. In Claude, click your name at the bottom left, then Settings.

    Download the zip

  2. 2

    Open Skills and click Add

    Under Customize, choose Skills. Click Add, then Upload a skill.

  3. 3

    Drop in a skill file

    Drag the skill's file into the box, or click to browse. You can add several at once.

  4. 4

    Pick the skill from the pack

    In the pack folder, open skills, then the skill you want, and select its SKILL.md — pmg-write-product-vision is a good first one.

  5. 5

    Check the preview and upload

    Claude shows the skill's name and what it does. Click Upload.

  6. 6

    Make sure it is switched on

    The skill opens on its own page. Its toggle should be on.

  7. 7

    Try it in a new chat

    Type / and the skill's name, then say what you need.

Then try one

Run pmg-write-product-vision for [product]. What we have so far: [paste it here]
Run pmg-synthesise-interviews on these interview transcripts: [paste them here]
Run pmg-score-with-rice on these requests: [paste them here]

06Standards

The quality bar

Every skill in the pack holds the same standard, the one we hold when we run our own product:

  • One framework, applied properly: each skill uses the real mechanics of its method — the scales, the grid, the formula, the order of the pass — not a generic gather, analyse, recommend
  • It tells you where it breaks: every skill says when not to use it, and which skill in the guide fits instead
  • Same shape every time: a fixed output template, and a short done-when check before handover
  • No invented facts: no made-up quotes, customers, market numbers, ROI figures or findings — missing data becomes a bracketed placeholder or an open question
  • Work is scored, people are not: skills score requests, ideas, options, risks and key results, never team members or individual users, and personas are composites rather than profiles of real people
  • A named person decides: the skill drafts the document and sets out the trade-off, the call and the send stay with the person who owns them
  • The red line: real customers are not optional — Claude drafts the documents, the team talks to users, and a named person makes the call

07FAQ

Questions people ask

What is in the Complete Claude Guide for Product Managers pack?

42 Claude skills that follow the product job in eight stages: set direction, discover, decide, define, deliver, launch, prove, and run the product. Each skill is named as an action and keeps one framework inside, with a fixed output template.

How do I install these Claude skills?

In Claude Code, two lines install all 42 at once. In Claude.ai or Claude Desktop, download the zip, open Settings, Skills, Add, and upload the skills you want. Either way it takes about five minutes.

Do I need Claude Code to use them?

No. The skills work in Claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code. In the app you upload them yourself; in Claude Code one command installs the whole pack.

Do the skills work with ChatGPT or other assistants?

They are built as Claude Skills, and installing them is a Claude feature. Each one is a plain Markdown file, so you can read it and reuse the method elsewhere, but it will not load and trigger by itself outside Claude.

Will Claude decide what we build?

No. Real customers are not optional. Claude drafts the documents, the team talks to users, and a named person makes the call. Work is scored, people are not.

Is the pack free?

Yes. It is free to use inside your company and in client work, and not for resale. There is no signup: the download and the install command are on this page.
